cohort: The study included 64 patients seeking permanent surgical contraception, divided into groups based on their preference for vaginal or laparoscopic salpingectomy.
finding: Both vaginal and laparoscopic salpingectomy were found to be feasible with low complication rates; vaginal salpingectomy had a significantly shorter mean surgical time, while laparoscopic salpingectomy showed significantly less intraoperative blood loss and fewer hospitalization hours.
